standard_language: Ordinary typed mathematical language: logical connectives, quantifiers, equality, sets, functions, tuples, finite indices and their usual notation. A type explicitly named natural numbers, integers, rationals, reals or complex numbers means that standard structure, with its usual numerals and arithmetic operations; these operation tokens need not be redeclared as project objects. The fixed finite calculation rules below, including a+0=a, are controller permissions, not an author claim. The core symbol table below is not a dictionary of all allowed mathematics. Objects and notation from any subject are introduced by this problem's parameters, D definitions or scoped locals, with their types and dependencies. Their properties need direct inputs or displayed local proofs; a familiar name or symbol supplies no theorem.

definitions.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
Ple_N f has coefficients 1_(|k|<=N)*hat f(k), N>=0; Pgt_N=I-Ple_N. These are used only in the proof and in initial-data approximation.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

definitions.type: smooth-input trilinear averaged cubic remainder with a polynomial dense core
definitions.definition: For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.

For an interval I with length at most one, X(I) consists of L^infinity(I;L^2) functions with weak time derivative in L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)); ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L^2))+||f'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). All time suprema of continuous functions use their continuous representatives; derivatives and L^infinity norms use essential suprema.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

inputs.statement: The following estimates have constants uniform in the real time t. For mean-zero f in L^2, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2. For any A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). For f,g in L^2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0 with Dinv A0 in L^2 and g in L^2, ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2 and ||J_t(A0,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2. For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Ctri_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise and sum across internal endpoints for continuous piecewise smooth paths. For time-independent mean-zero f,g, Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t). The bounded products extend from polynomials by density.

inputs.statement: With normalized norms, for every interval I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b<=a+1 and continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero paths f_j, ||Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C|I|product_j||f_j||_(X(I))+C||f_i||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)))product_(j!=i)||f_j||_(L^infinity(I;L^2)), for each slot i=1,2,3. For time-independent mean-zero H^sigma inputs, 0<=sigma<=1, ||Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C_sigma|I|^sigma product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma). For 0<gamma<=1 set a_gamma=1/2-gamma when gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 when gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 when gamma>1/2. Then a_gamma in [0,1), ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)). For every M0>=0, mean-zero w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, 0<tau<=1, a>=0, and a<=t<=a+tau, ||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma and ||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0). Constants are uniform in a,t,tau and Fourier support. Ctri and stages extend by their stated bounds.

inputs.statement: For 0<gamma<=1, M0>=1, a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero real f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, put q=tau^gamma+delta and (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y)=Interp_(a,tau;f), I=[a,a+tau]. Constants C_(gamma,M0) below are uniform in a,tau and all higher norms or spectral supports. Then ||f||_2<=M0+1, q<=2, sup_I||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta, sup_I(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, ||z||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, sup_I||Q||_2+||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and sup_I||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Here a_gamma is 1/2-gamma,1/8,0 in the respective cases gamma<1/2, gamma=1/2, gamma>1/2. Moreover Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau, sup_I||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, sup_I||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f), sup_I||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, and sup_I||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

For 0<gamma<=1, M0>=1, a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero real f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and ||f-w||_2<=1, put q=tau^gamma+||f-w||_2 and take the tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y)=Interp_(a,tau;f); define rho(t)=-integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds-(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(Y,Y)ds-((t-a)/tau)*W on [a,a+tau]. Then Vst'=(1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst)+rho', rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau, sup||rho||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. On a smooth numerical trajectory and smooth exact twisted solution v with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, concatenate these increments into Rres(0)=0, and let V be its continuous concatenation with grid values V(t_n)=v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. Then V'=(1/2)B_t(V,V)+Rres'. If I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, including an endpoint inside a step, one has sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0). The constants are independent of grid index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

binders.type: smooth exact twisted path satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v)

output.statement: Fix 0<gamma<=1 and M0>=1. There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0, depending only on gamma,M0, with the following property. For any 0<tau<=delta0/2, any smooth real mean-zero exact twisted path v satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and any smooth real mean-zero numerical trajectory with interpolation V obtained from Interp at its grid values, let e=v-V. On every interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=delta0 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, one has E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. The endpoint b may lie inside a step. More precisely the proof gives for all N>=2,h<=1,0<tau<=1 under this bootstrap: e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds; sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I; F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds; sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I; and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Here Rres is the concatenation of the step increments rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)W_n, where the subscripted tuple is Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n), with Rres(0)=0, and every constant is independent of time index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

locals.declaration: Fix 0<tau<=1, with the smaller final restriction imposed later.
Fix the exact twisted path v.
Fix the interpolation V of the specified numerical trajectory.
Fix a grid starting point a.
Use the concatenated step residual defined by N009.
Fix an arbitrary proof-only threshold N>=2.
Let Hproj be the identity operator minus Lproj.
Choose C0>=1 dominating the finite constants in F005, uniformly over admissible intervals and trajectories.

argument.text: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. Assume L1: the smooth real mean-zero v satisfies v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and the numerical interpolation V is taken on an interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, E_I<=1. Set e=v-V,g=v-e/2 and take the concatenated Rres from N009. Its conclusions apply to this trajectory and give the accumulated residual and X bounds. In particular e'=B_t(e,g)-Rres', so integration gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Also ||e||_X<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||v||_X+||V||_X+||g||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

Fix N>=2 only in the proof. For each time s, the inverse-product bound of N005 and the Fourier inequality ||Ple_N partial_x^2 A||_2<=N^2||A||_2 give ||Ple_N B_s(e,g)||_2<=C*N^2||e||_2||g||_2. Indeed B_s(e,g)=S_(-s)partial_x^2 Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]. Integrate over length at most h and use bounded ||g||_2 to obtain sup||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, for every N>=2, sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

argument.text: Apply the two-endpoint normal form N005 to F_I. The equations give e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)B(v,v)-(1/2)B(e,g)+(1/2)Rres'. In the differentiated J terms, its symmetry and integral J(B,h)=Ctri give Ctri(e,g,g)-(1/2)Ctri(e,g,e)=Ctri(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is (1/2)Ctri(v,v,e), and the forcing terms satisfy -J(Rres',g)+(1/2)J(e,Rres')=-J(Rres',V). Multiplication by -1/3 yields F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Both endpoints are retained. Apply the H^1 bound for J in N005: their projections above N are <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I. Continuity of all the paths makes internal endpoints cancel when the normal form is applied stepwise.

produces.statement: Under L1, F_I(t)=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. The sum of the norms of Pgt_N J_t(e,g) and Pgt_N J_a(e,g) is <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three admissible paths on I, put Lproj=Ple_(N/3),Hproj equal to the identity operator minus Lproj. The telescoping expansion Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)-Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Lproj f_3)=Ctri(Hproj f_1,f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Hproj f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Hproj f_3) places a high input in each term. The all-low term has no output above N because all product frequencies sum. Each projection contracts both components of X and ||Hproj f_i||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||f_i||_2 by Fourier weights. Apply N006 with the negative norm on that particular high slot. This proves ||Pgt_N Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infinity L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), using F001: their total contribution is <=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)||_2+||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I uniformly for t in I.

argument.text: For the remaining integral in F003 substitute the actual stepwise Rres' formula from N009, and use integral J(B,h)=Ctri from N005 on each intersected step segment. It becomes -Ctri(Y_n,z_n,V)-(1/2)Ctri(Y_n,Y_n,V)-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds. At that step's start, delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C*q_n, ||Y_n||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C and ||W_n||_2<=C*tau*q_n. N006, with the negative norm on Y_n, bounds the first two terms by C*tau*q_n (using q_n<=2 and ||V||_X<=C from F001). The last term is also <=C*tau*q_n by the L^2 J bound from N005. These remain valid upper bounds on a partial final step. At most h/tau+1 steps are met, and q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I. Thus the forcing integral is bounded by C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(t in I)||integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). All constants in this bound and the endpoint, cubic, low-frequency and accumulated residual bounds can be dominated by a single positive constant depending only on gamma,M0, uniformly over admissible trajectories, intervals, timesteps and thresholds N>=2.

argument.text: Combine F003-F005 to obtain sup||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. With F002, the exact error identity and residual bound in F001 give E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All constants are uniform in the parameters specified in F005.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, with one constant depending only on gamma,M0.

argument.text: Choose C0>=1 dominating these constants from F005-F006, independently of all the particular paths. Define N0=ceil(max(2,16*C0,(16*C0)^(1/pstar))). Then C0*(N0^(-1)+N0^(-pstar))<=1/8<=1/4. Put delta0=min(1,1/(8*C0*(N0^2+3))) and K0=4*C0. If h<=delta0 and tau<=delta0/2, then C0*(N0^2*h+h+tau)<=C0*delta0*(N0^2+3)<=1/8<=1/4. F006 therefore has E_I coefficient at most 1/2. Absorption gives E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+2*C0*(h+tau)*tau^gamma<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. These choices depend only on gamma,M0. Discharge L1, retaining its antecedents in the conditional theorem, and quantify all trajectories, intervals and timesteps. This proves the output assertion.
